Nithin Goutham THESIS "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003ETHESIS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFACTORS INFLUENCING RECOVERY OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH RESPIRATORY FAILURE\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINTRODUCTION:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe respiratory system allows gas exchange between the environment and the body, facilitating the process of aerobic metabolism. Specifically, the respiratory system provides oxygen and removes carbon dioxide from the body. The inability of the respiratory system to perform either or both of these tasks results in respiratory failure. Type 1 respiratory failure occurs when the respiratory system cannot adequately provide oxygen to the body, leading to hypoxemia. Type 2 respiratory failure occurs when the respiratory system cannot sufficiently remove carbon dioxide from the body, leading to hypercapnia.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERespiratory failure can be classified based on chronicity (i.e., acute, chronic, and acute on chronic). A thorough understanding of respiratory failure is crucial to managing this disorder. If either type of respiratory failure is not identified and addressed early, it will become life-threatening and lead to respiratory arrest, coma, and death. 1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAcute respiratory failure due to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) ranges in incidence from 10-80\/100,000\/y based on where it is recorded worldwide. This is partly due t different practices and thresholds for intubation in these cases and the use of different definitions of ARDs. According to one report, it is estimated that 10% of all patients admitted to ICU and 23% of mechanically ventilated patients meet ARDS criteria.(2)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAcute respiratory failure related to Coronavirus (COVID-19): It is estimated early in the COVID-19 pandemic that up to 79% of hospitalized patients developed respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation.(3)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAcute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD) is the third most common etiology in patients hospitalized because of acute respiratory failure.(4)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPROBLEM STATEMENT\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; Respiratory failure is a leading cause of mortality and morbidity and in recent times the pandemic of covid has heightened awareness around this problem where there has been increased numbers of ECMO, lung transplants and while many were justified there were many instances where the necessary care was suboptimal.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUnderstanding factors influencing outcomes in patients with Respiratory Failure is important to optimize better care for such patients.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAIM\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETO ASSESS\u0026nbsp; THE VARIOUS FACTORS INFLUENCING RECOVERY OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH RESPIRATORY FAILURE SPECTRUM SEEN IN THE MEDICINE DEPARTMENT.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOBJECTIVES\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) To identify the spectrum of respiratory failure patients coming to general medicine department.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)To study the clinical, radiological and laboratory profile of the spectrum of respiratory failure patients coming to general medicine department\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)To assess the various factors influencing the causation and recovery of respiratory failure in those patients.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESTUDY DESIGN :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EProspective study design with analysis of factors influencing the outcome of the patients with Respiratory Failure.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINCLUSION CRITERIA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) Patients above the age of 18 years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) Patients with Common causes of respiratory failure like pneumonia, pulmonary edema, pulmonary embolism, acute respiratory distress syndrome, atelectasis, asthma, COPD, neuromuscular and chest wall disorders, inadequate post-operative analgesia, smoking, obesity,\u0026nbsp; shock, heart failure, cardiac arrhythmia and lung cancer.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEXCLUSION CRITERIA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) Patients under the age of 18 years\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) Patients\/Patients attendants who are not willing for study or not giving consent for the purpose of study\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) Patients without any factors or conditions influencing respiratory failure.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPATIENTS AND METHODOLOGY\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPLACE OF STUDY: Department of General medicine, Kamineni institute of medical sciences, Narketpally.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESTUDY PERIOD: April 2023- March 2025\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESTUDY DESIGN : Prospective Observational Qualitative study.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESAMPLE SIZE: Proposed No. of cases to be studied = 50\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECASE PROFORMA\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
